from dspy.adapters.types.tool import ToolCalls

# Case 1: dict with tool_calls (canonical)
print('1:', ToolCalls.validate_input({'tool_calls': [{'name': 'foo', 'args': {'a': 1}}]}))

# Case 2: single object without tool_calls
print('2:', ToolCalls.validate_input({'name': 'foo', 'args': {'a': 1}}))

# Case 3: bare list
print('3:', ToolCalls.validate_input([{'name': 'foo', 'args': {}}, {'name': 'bar', 'args': {}}]))

# Case 4: JSON string (single object)
print('4:', ToolCalls.validate_input('{\"name\": \"foo\", \"args\": {\"a\": 1}}'))

# Case 5: JSON string (list)
print('5:', ToolCalls.validate_input('[{\"name\": \"foo\", \"args\": {}}]'))

# Case 6: JSON string (tool_calls)
print('6:', ToolCalls.validate_input('{\"tool_calls\": [{\"name\": \"foo\", \"args\": {}}]}'))

# Case 7: non-JSON string
print('7:', ToolCalls.validate_input('not json at all'))

# Case 8: constructing a ToolCalls instance from each format
tc1 = ToolCalls({'name': 'foo', 'args': {'a': 1}})
print('8a:', tc1)
tc2 = ToolCalls([{'name': 'foo', 'args': {}}, {'name': 'bar', 'args': {}}])
print('8b:', tc2)
tc3 = ToolCalls({'tool_calls': [{'name': 'foo', 'args': {}}]})
print('8c:', tc3)
tc4 = ToolCalls('{\"name\": \"foo\", \"args\": {\"a\": 1}}')
print('8d:', tc4)
tc5 = ToolCalls('[{\"name\": \"foo\", \"args\": {}}]')
print('8e:', tc5)
